summary: TradeQuest iteration_5 — Watchlist feature (star favorites, pinned to top). Backend: 11/11 pytest passed in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration_5_watchlist.py. POST /api/watchlist/{symbol}/toggle correctly adds symbol on first call (returns {symbol, in_watchlist:true, watchlist:[...]}), removes on second, normalizes lowercase input (msft→MSFT), returns 404 for invalid symbol (ZZZZZ), and is auth-gated (401 without JWT). GET /api/stocks: every item includes in_watchlist bool, and watchlisted symbols are pinned to the top of the list (verified after toggling 2 non-adjacent symbols — both appear at indices 0 & 1). GET /api/stocks/{symbol}: in_watchlist flips correctly with toggle. Persistence verified via re-login as same user (fresh JWT) → watchlist still contains TSLA and TSLA still pinned at top of /api/stocks. Category filter (?category=Tech) and search (?q=app) still return in_watchlist on every item — no regression. Frontend (390x844 mobile viewport, 3 separate signup+agree sessions): Explore tab renders 16 stock cards, each with a testID='watch-toggle-{SYMBOL}' star. Tapping the star (a) does NOT navigate to detail (regression pass — Pressable.onPress on star does not bubble into card Pressable), (b) moves the stock to the top under a WATCHLIST section header (with amber star icon), (c) shows an 'ALL STOCKS' section header for the rest. Both headers only appear when watchedCount>0 (confirmed hidden by default). Stock detail top bar (testID='watch-toggle-{SYMBOL}') toggles state — after starring MSFT/NVDA from detail and returning to Explore, that stock is pinned to top with gold star. Full page RELOAD (browser refresh) preserves the pinned WATCHLIST — NVDA remained at index 0 with WATCHLIST header still shown, proving persistence via user.watchlist in MongoDB. Search + category filter behave normally.

react_native_issues.issue: Duplicate testID collision on web: when the stock detail screen is open, Expo Router keeps the previous Explore screen mounted in the DOM, so [data-testid="watch-toggle-{SYMBOL}"] matches TWO elements — the hidden card star from Explore AND the visible top-bar star from detail. Playwright's page.click() on the shared selector fails with 'Element is not visible' (picks the hidden one). This is a testability/accessibility concern; on native it is fine, but web testing has to resort to querying all matches and clicking the last. Recommendation: rename detail-screen star testID to 'watch-toggle-detail-{SYMBOL}' (or scope card stars as 'watch-toggle-card-{SYMBOL}'). Reference: /app/frontend/app/stock/[symbol].tsx:71 and /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/explore.tsx:215

critical_code_review_comments: POST /api/watchlist/{symbol}/toggle correctly uppercases input and validates against STOCK_MAP before touching the DB (returns 404 for unknown symbols). Watchlist mutation uses $set with the full list — idempotent and safe.

GET /api/stocks pins watchlisted items via 'out.sort(key=lambda x: not x["in_watchlist"])' — Python's sort is stable, so the relative order of watchlisted items and of non-watchlisted items is preserved from STOCKS[] order. This matched observed frontend behavior.
Frontend Explore optimistically flips in_watchlist locally before awaiting the API, and rolls back on error (explore.tsx:80-99) — good UX + resilient.

Section headers use showWatchHeader = watchedCount>0 && index===0 and showAllHeader = watchedCount>0 && index===watchedCount — clean, correct, and only render when at least one stock is watchlisted (matches spec).

Star Pressable in Explore is nested INSIDE the card Pressable but its onPress does NOT bubble to the parent card — verified by testing (tapping star did not open detail). React Native handles inner-Pressable capture correctly on web here.
Stock detail toggleWatch is optimistic + rollback on error (stock/[symbol].tsx:46-55). Uses Haptics.impactAsync — no-ops on web as expected.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of exercisable flows: signup → agreement → Explore → toggle star (list) → detail star toggle → back → verify pinned order → full page reload → verify persistence → category + search regression
